compiled_state.description:
## The gap

`rebar/host` publishes three liveness heartbeats — `gerrit_healthy`, `reviewbot_healthy`,
`mcp_healthy` — and **`gerrit_healthy` and `reviewbot_healthy` have NO CloudWatch alarm at all.**

Verified directly:

```
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms \
  --query 'MetricAlarms[?MetricName==`gerrit_healthy`||MetricName==`reviewbot_healthy`]'
-> (empty)
```

Twenty-two `rebar/host` alarms exist, covering disk, docker storage, journal, memory-abort,
buildkit cache, gate scratch, bridge failures, voter errors, replication and mirror sync. The two
signals that answer "is the review system alive at all" are published, look reassuring on a
dashboard, and are watched by nobody.

## Observed cost, 2026-09-05

During a real Gerrit degradation that failed the checkout step of THREE changes with HTTP 504
(`ergophobic-harassed-peacock`, `1e24-bfc0-5f70-4ea4`), `gerrit_healthy` published **nothing for
over 30 minutes** while `mem_used_percent` from the same probe tick published normally. So the
probe was alive and its Gerrit health check specifically could not complete — exactly the
condition worth paging on — and nothing fired.

The degradation was found by a human reading CI failure logs and correlating them by hand. The
metric that would have named it directly sat unwatched.

## Why silence here is the dangerous direction

These are heartbeats: `1` means healthy, and the interesting state is ABSENCE. An unalarmed
heartbeat is strictly worse than no heartbeat, because it creates the appearance of coverage. It is
the same shape this project has already fixed elsewhere — `bff5-9163` established that every
`rebar/host` alarm must treat missing data as `breaching` precisely so a dead publisher pages
instead of reading as healthy. That work fixed the alarms that EXIST. It could not fix a metric
that has no alarm at all, and this is the residue.

Note the asymmetry with `mcp_healthy`: also unalarmed here, but the MCP has adjacent coverage
(`mcp_retire_cap`, `mcp_mem_abort`). Gerrit and the review bot have no such proxy — if they stop,
the only signal is that changes stop moving, which is indistinguishable from a quiet night.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gerrit_healthy` and `reviewbot_healthy` each have an alarm that fires on missing data
      (`treat_missing_data = "breaching"`) and on an unhealthy value, SNS-wired like the others.
- [ ] The windows are wide enough not to flap on a single missed probe tick, and that is proven by
      replaying each metric's own recorded series against the proposed configuration — the method
      `bff5-9163` AC2 established, not by waiting a day to see.
- [ ] The guard test in `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` is extended so that a
      `rebar/host` metric which is a LIVENESS HEARTBEAT cannot exist without an alarm. Today's
      guard checks that alarms which exist are correct; it cannot notice a metric nobody watches.
      Proven by deliberately adding a heartbeat metric with no alarm and seeing the test fail.
- [ ] The full `rebar/host` metric list is swept once against the alarm list, and every unalarmed
      metric is either given an alarm or recorded with a reason. Enumerate the result — do not fix
      only the two named here.
compiled_state.title: gerrit_healthy and reviewbot_healthy have NO alarm at all: gerrit_healthy went dark for 30+ minutes during a real degradation that blocked every landing, and nothing fired
